learningObjectives: Separate technical models from test actions and expectations.
Start and inspect a local XBrowser scan.
Choose stable identifiers without universal anchor guarantees.
Convert eligible same-type controls to a group.

elements.text: Modules store technical information; TestSteps supply actions and values. Reusing models can reduce duplicated maintenance, while meaningful naming makes tests easier to read. Scanning alone does not create business expectations, select all test data or guarantee working tests after an application change.
Independent guidance: update a shared model deliberately, inspect dependent TestSteps and rerun affected assertions. A reference update is not proof of application correctness.

elements.text: Modules can come from scanning, the Standard subset, recording or manual creation. In scanned Modules, ModuleAttributes represent selected controls; in Standard Modules they can be execution-task parameters. A ModuleAttribute is not merely a property such as the Module name.

Creating a TestStep creates TestStepValues from those ModuleAttributes. Fill the values and action modes to express test intent. Model properties identify and steer supported objects; not every automation operation imitates a human UI interaction.

Standard.tsu provides ready-made XModules, sample TestCases/ExecutionLists, virtual folders and report templates. Import it during workspace creation or into an existing workspace using the supported procedure.

Independent guidance: choose a compatible utility or engine operation and configure its parameters. A pre-built Module does not make every action independent of the application or guarantee unrestricted use across versions.
For local XBrowser scanning, prepare the target browser extension. Start from a Module folder with Scan → Application or Ctrl+Shift+A, then choose the application in Select Application and scan it.

Select controls in the scan result or use Select on Screen. Review uniqueness, rename models and save the scan results. Use Advanced View when accessibility features are needed; Basic/Condensed View do not support them.
Use descriptive Module names; the naming guide suggests application | general section | coverage. Independent example: WebShop | Checkout | Payment. A naming separator is not an identifier.

A wildcard can tolerate a dynamic suffix in an identification property. Independent example: Demo Web Shop* may match related titles, but also multiple windows; inspect uniqueness and actual controls rather than assuming one broad title makes every page compatible.

elements.text: Scan an authorized disposable page, select a small functional set of controls and inspect unique identifiers. Define expected actions separately. Original Academy Exercise 03 was inaccessible; no actual XScan execution occurred.

Properties are the default identification method. Try a stable unique combination first; Make Unique can add identifying properties. Parent context can disambiguate repeated controls and is not necessarily the immediate parent. Index and image identification are additional options, but ordering or appearance changes can affect them.

Anchors identify a target relative to another identifiable control. The current best-practice guide recommends anchors only for non-web applications because stable anchors can be difficult in modern web UIs. A dynamic web ID alone is not a reason to skip stable properties and parent context.

ShortestPath searches outward through tree levels from the anchor’s children. Coordinate uses the anchor position and a search angle. Auto is the default: it tries ShortestPath, then Coordinate on failure. None of these names guarantees stability under every DOM, layout or resolution change.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Convert eligible controls to a ControlGroup

elements.text: Select eligible ModuleAttributes and choose Convert to ControlGroup. Only controls of the same type can be grouped; the documented eligible types are radio buttons, buttons and links. Existing TestCase use or unavailable checkout can prevent conversion.
Grouped TestStepValues offer controls through a dropdown. This simplifies choosing a member; it does not automatically execute every grouped control with one action.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing technical model and expected result
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a scan defines correct business outcomes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Supply explicit actions, data and expected assertions.

examPitfalls.title: Universal data claims
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming MBTA always generates business data or never supports any defaulting feature.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Model reuse alone does not supply valid test data; check the specific data feature.

examPitfalls.title: ModuleAttribute is not Module metadata
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Scanned attributes represent controls; standard ones can be task parameters.

examPitfalls.title: Pre-built does not mean unconfigured
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating Standard Modules as universally application-independent.

examPitfalls.title: Parent context vs menu count
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming five techniques mean five separate ribbon commands.

examPitfalls.title: Anchor guarantees
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming dynamic web IDs mandate anchors or ShortestPath cannot fail.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Try stable properties/context first; Auto can fall back to Coordinate.

examPitfalls.title: Scan scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Applying local Chrome extension guidance to every engine.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the selected engine and target environment.

examPitfalls.title: ControlGroup restrictions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Grouping mixed types or assuming one action operates all members.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Convert eligible same-type controls and choose the intended member.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How does this model-based workflow organize reusable technical information and test intent?

options.text: It guarantees autonomous repair of every failed test.
It necessarily compiles UML into native machine code.
It only documents manual tests.
Modules describe technical objects; TestSteps provide actions and data using those models.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Reusable technical models are used by test actions; scanning does not invent every expected business result.

optionExplanations.B: No native compilation guarantee is established.
optionExplanations.C: Models support automation rather than only documentation.
optionExplanations.D: This separates model information and test intent.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which THREE are potential benefits of reusable well-named scanned models?

options.text: Reduced effort from reusing scanned technical information.
Readable intent when names and actions are meaningful.
Less duplicated model maintenance.
Model reuse automatically supplies every valid business dataset.
Every model always executes faster than scripted tests.

practiceQuiz.hint: Benefits depend on design; guarantees are different.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Reuse can support effort, readability and maintenance; it does not guarantee data or execution speed.

optionExplanations.A: Reuse can reduce repeated modeling work.
optionExplanations.C: Centralized model reuse can reduce duplication.
optionExplanations.D: Correct data must be designed or supplied through an appropriate feature.
optionExplanations.E: No universal speed comparison is supported.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a scanned Module, what represents the selected button or field technically?

options.text: A ModuleAttribute representing that control.
The entire TestCase execution sequence.
An execution log entry.
Only Module-level metadata such as its name.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Scanned ModuleAttributes represent controls and produce corresponding TestStepValues.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented scanned-object representation.
optionExplanations.B: A sequence uses models rather than representing one control.
optionExplanations.C: Logs record execution rather than define this model entry.
optionExplanations.D: Module metadata is not the selected control representation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a learner obtain compatible ready-made utility Modules without scanning their own UI?

options.text: Assume utility operations cannot be automated.
Rescan an unrelated page repeatedly.
Assume Commander requires JavaScript for every utility.
Import the applicable Standard subset and configure the selected Module.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Pre-built operations are supplied in the Standard subset.

optionExplanations.B: An unrelated UI scan does not create the toolkit.
optionExplanations.C: Every utility does not require custom scripting.
optionExplanations.D: This obtains and configures the existing operation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does scanning a supported GUI with XScan create?

options.text: A technical model from selected controls and identification information.
A certificate that the application is secure.
A guaranteed passing result for every test.
A complete business oracle without specifying expected behavior.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The scan prepares technical information used by TestSteps.

optionExplanations.B: It is not a security certification.
optionExplanations.C: Models do not guarantee test outcomes.
optionExplanations.D: Business expectations remain a testing responsibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which is a documented XScan launch method?

options.text: Assume a Go to → XScan command.
Right-click a Module folder → Scan → Application, then choose the application.
File → New → XScan Session for all releases.
Assume every project automatically starts scanning.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Application scanning can be started from a Module folder.

optionExplanations.A: The asserted command is not the documented path.
optionExplanations.C: No universal File command is established.
optionExplanations.D: Opening a project does not imply this scan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A web control has a changing ID. What should you investigate before choosing fragile identification?

options.text: Use the full changing ID unchanged.
Give up because dynamic controls are impossible.
Try a stable unique property combination and appropriate parent context.
Match every possible ID with a broad wildcard and assume uniqueness.

practiceQuiz.hint: The dynamic ID is not the only available information.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Current web best practice prioritizes stable properties and parent context rather than automatically selecting anchors.

optionExplanations.A: An unstable full ID may fail on the next run.
optionExplanations.D: A broad match does not establish uniqueness.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A web button has an inspected stable unique identifier. Which initial technique is suitable?

options.text: Always use anchors because they can never change.
Rescan repeatedly without checking identity.
Always replace the unique identifier with coordinates.
Use the stable property and verify identification in the intended environment.

optionExplanations.B: Repeated scanning alone does not improve identity.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which FIVE identification techniques/context mechanisms are discussed in this lesson, rather than five separate ribbon commands?

options.text: Title alone as a separate method
Properties
Parent context
URL alone as a separate method
View as an identification method
Anchor
Image
Index

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish property values from techniques and context.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Properties, parent context, anchors, images and index are discussed; a Title or URL value can participate in properties without being its own method.

optionExplanations.A: A title is a possible property, not this separate technique.
optionExplanations.C: Parent context can scope ambiguous matches.
optionExplanations.D: A URL value is not a standalone method here.
optionExplanations.E: A view configures scanning UI rather than identity.
optionExplanations.H: Index disambiguates matching candidates by position.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For an applicable anchor identification, which algorithm searches tree levels instead of using the anchor’s coordinates and search angle?

options.text: ShortestPath
Coordinate
Both always use only exact pixels
Neither supports tree searching

practiceQuiz.hint: Describe the algorithm rather than promise stability.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ShortestPath searches from anchor children through tree levels; Auto can fall back to Coordinate.

optionExplanations.B: Coordinate uses position and a search angle.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An identification property has a dynamic suffix after Demo Web Shop. Which candidate value tolerates that suffix while still requiring a uniqueness check?

options.text: Leave all identifiers empty and assume a unique target.
Demo Web Shop*; inspect whether multiple windows or controls also match.
Use unsupported semicolon concatenation and assume each title is selected.
Assume identifier wildcards cannot be used.

practiceQuiz.hint: Tolerating a suffix is not proving uniqueness.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A wildcard can handle a dynamic suffix but may broaden the match.

optionExplanations.A: Empty identifiers do not prove a unique target.
optionExplanations.B: This handles the suffix while keeping validation explicit.
optionExplanations.C: No such concatenation rule is established.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Seven eligible same-type links are not yet used in TestCases. How can their ModuleAttributes be organized for dropdown member selection?

options.text: An unrelated TestSuite automatically groups controls.
One Module per link is mandatory.
Select the eligible attributes and use Convert to ControlGroup.
An ExecutionList converts every control into one automatic click.

practiceQuiz.rationale: ControlGroup organizes eligible attributes and exposes member selection, not automatic execution of all links.

optionExplanations.A: A TestSuite is not this Module conversion.
optionExplanations.B: Separate Modules are not mandatory for this grouping.
optionExplanations.D: Execution scheduling does not perform this conversion or click all members.
